evidence_spans: Moreover, we investigated the type of mobile dislocations using the neutron diffraction (ND) peak-broadening modeling and analysis using the Williamson-Hall plot method ( [17] ), experimentally verified by the high-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) technique.
It is found that the dominant type of mobile dislocations during plastic deformation could be edge dislocations, which is different from conventional BCC metals.

intervention.action: in situ neutron diffraction during elastic deformation
intervention.description: Lattice strain evolution measured along axial and transverse directions for different {hkl} planes

structure.description: Single BCC solid solution with grains of different orientations

evidence_units.mechanism: At higher temperatures, reduced overall stiffness leads to increased elastic anisotropy, causing different slopes in lattice strain versus applied stress for different crystallographic orientations

outcome.measurement_method: slope of lattice strain evolution versus applied stress

evidence_spans: The slope of the lattice strain evolution versus applied stress, during elastic deformation, determines the diffraction elastic constants for the specific { hkl } planes.
It was found that the variation in diffraction elastic constants among all the grains is not clearly observed, indicating the elastically isotropic deformation behavior, as presented in Fig. 2A .

Unlike the lattice strain evolution at RT, different slopes in the lattice strains versus applied stresses at elevated temperatures are observed due to the increased elastic anisotropy, as presented in Fig. 2 (B to D) .
At higher temperatures, where the overall stiffness is reduced, the anisotropy increases.

intervention.action: in situ neutron diffraction and mechanical testing
intervention.description: Applied stress to measure lattice strain evolution and determine elastic moduli

structure.description: Single BCC solid-solution phase with nearly identical elastic moduli in differently oriented grains

evidence_units.mechanism: The BCC-structured material exhibits no orientation-dependent lattice strain evolutions during elastic deformation, leading to nearly similar values of elastic moduli in differently oriented grains and eliminating the typical sequence of grain yielding based on elastic stiffness or Schmid factor.

outcome.property: elastic isotropy (Zener anisotropy ratio Az and Voigt-Reuss bound AVR)

evidence_spans: Unlike conventional BCC alloys, as discussed above, the NbTaTiV BCC refractory HEA exhibits no orientation-dependent lattice strain evolutions during elastic deformation at RT, leading to nearly similar values of elastic moduli in differently grains, as presented in Fig. 2A .

intervention.description: Applied stress until yielding occurred in all grains

evidence_units.mechanism: The unusual elastic isotropy causes all oriented grains to yield at the same stress level rather than the typical grain-to-grain yielding sequence based on orientation-dependent stiffness.
evidence_spans: With this unusual elastic deformation, all orientated grains yield at the same stress level (around 1000 MPa), as presented in fig. S2.

structure.description: Dominant mobile dislocations are <111> {110} edge dislocations

evidence_units.mechanism: Severe lattice distortion causes edge dislocation cores to deviate from neutral dislocation planes, producing wavy dislocation lines and reducing edge dislocation mobility, making them comparable in number to screw dislocations and dominant in this BCC HEA.

comparison.baseline_state: screw dislocations dominant due to easy edge annihilation

evidence_spans: These results clearly indicate that the type of mobile dislocations of the NbTaTiV refractory HEA is edge dislocations in the initial condition (nondeformed) at elevated temperatures.
Moreover, with increasing macrostrains (up to 15% deformed), the <111> {110} edge dislocation remains as a dominant mobile dislocation character at RT and elevated temperatures ( Fig. 5, B to D ).

Similar to the above reported prediction, the dominant mobile dislocations of the investigated NbTaTiV BCC refractory HEA, which has severely distorted lattices, are close to <111> {110} edge dislocations with increasing macrostrain, as presented in Fig 5B .

intervention.action: plastic deformation with load transfer monitoring
intervention.description: Deformed at RT to monitor intergranular load transfer

structure.description: Reduced plastic anisotropy with homogeneous load sharing

evidence_units.mechanism: The reduced plastic anisotropy leads to homogeneous load sharing between differently oriented grains rather than load concentration on particular grains, preventing stress concentrations.

comparison.baseline_state: strong load transfer and stress concentration

evidence_spans: Furthermore, the features of the load transfer were not clearly presented during plastic deformation at RT, indicating the reduced plastic anisotropy.

This trend of the reduced plastic anisotropic deformation behavior could result in the excellent ductility (plasticity) at RT because of the homogeneous load sharing between differently grains rather than the load concentration on particular grains during plastic deformation, as shown in fig. S2.

intervention.description: Measured Zener anisotropy parameters (Az) at elevated temperatures

structure.description: Single BCC solid-solution phase maintained up to 900°C

evidence_units.mechanism: The NbTaTiV alloy exhibits a gradual increase in elastic anisotropy at elevated temperatures, but the variation in anisotropy parameters is much smaller than that observed in conventional alloys, indicating superior temperature stability of elastic isotropy.
evidence_spans: In case of the present NbTaTiV HEA, the Zener anisotropy parameters were gradually increased at elevated temperatures, but the variation of anisotropy parameters in NbTaTiV (1.2 at RT and 1.6 at 900°C) is much smaller than other conventional alloys ( [11] – [13] ).

The detailed comparisons of the Zener anisotropy parameters and yield strengths at elevated temperatures between the NFA ( [13] ) and the present NbTaTiV refractory HEA are indicated in fig. S3, manifesting that both alloys show the temperature-dependent elastic anisotropy and the smaller variation of the Zener anisotropy parameters in the NbTaTiV HEA than the nanostructured ferritic alloy at elevated temperatures.

evidence_spans: The compression experiments on the homogenization-treated NbTaTiV alloy with a diameter of 4 mm and a length of 8 mm were conducted to investigate the elastic and plastic deformation behaviors at RT and elevated temperatures using a mechanical testing system load frame.
During the elastic deformation period, a stepwise force control sequence was used by collecting the 20-min measurement time of ND data at each stress level.

When the stress level reached 1030 MPa for RT, 650 MPa for 500°C, 585 MPa for 700°C, and 550 MPa for 900°C (close to the macroscopic yield strength), a stepwise displacement control with an incremental step of 0.2 mm was used.

material.name: NbTaTiV alloy
material.composition: Nb 25 Ta 25 Ti 25 V 25 in atomic %
material.initial_state: 64-atom special quasirandom structure modeled using Monte Carlo–simulated annealing

intervention.description: Calculation of elastic tensor using distorted structures based on Green-Lagrange strain tensors

parameters.symmetry_correction: Projection technique to derive closest elastic tensors with cubic symmetry

structure.description: SQS supercell with cubic symmetry derived from projection

candidate.mechanism: A linear least-squares fit between the computed stress and strain tensors was performed to calculate the elastic tensor, followed by a projection technique to derive cubic symmetry elastic tensors from the non-symmetric SQS supercell.
evidence_spans: First-principles calculations were performed with the Vienna Ab-initio Simulation Package (VASP) using the projector augmented-wave (PAW) method ( [36] ).
The chemical disorder of the solid solution was modeled using a 64-atom special quasirandom structure (SQS).
The elastic tensor of the SQS supercell was calculated using a set of distorted structures based on the methodology described in ( [37] ).
The supercell's lattice parameters were fixed at the experimentally determined RT values, and the ionic positions were allowed to relax.
A set of deformed structures were generated by adopting 3 × 3 Green-Lagrange strain tensors of varying magnitudes at ±0.5 and ±1%.
For each distorted structure, the 3 × 3 stress tensor is computed by the DFT.
A linear least-squares fit between the stress and strain tensors was performed to calculate the elastic tensor of the SQS.

However, because the SQS supercell does not conserve the point-group symmetry, a projection technique is used to derive the closest elastic tensors with a cubic symmetry for the NbTaTiV alloy, which is equivalent to crystallographically averaging tensor elements.
